also: on your marks, get set, go

terms.comment: A starter’s call of ours from plain words: parātus, ready, and the imperative of currō; to one child, Parātus es? Curre!. Roman races started from the stalls, carcerēs, at a signal (signum), as in Ennius and Vergil (see the examples); we have found no set words for the start in the authors, Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini.

terms.gloss: on your marks, to the starting line
terms.comment: Of ours, with carcerēs, the starting stalls of the circus, which Cicero sets against calx, the finish line (Cic. Sen. 83); see “finish line”.

phrases.latin: haec ubi dicta, locum capiunt signōque repente corripiunt spatia audītō līmenque relinquunt
phrases.english: when this was said, they take their places, and at the signal, all at once, they dash down the course and leave the line

phrases.latin: exspectant, velutī cōnsul cum mittere signum volt, omnēs avidī spectant ad carceris ōrās
phrases.english: they wait, as when the consul is about to give the signal, and all watch eagerly the mouth of the starting gates
